subject: EU residency + APAC standby: renewal SOW & capacity readiness
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Popov <elena.popov@medica-eu.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: EU residency + APAC standby: renewal SOW & capacity readiness

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the productive renewal call last week. Per our discussion, I wanted to put next steps in writing so procurement and engineering have a single source of truth. High-level asks from your side:

- Confirm go-live window for EU primary (target: 2027-07-01)
- Confirm APAC standby behavior (warm-standby with failover within 90s)
- Commit to increased monthly reserved tokens for Q3 to support planned campaign (baseline + 40%)

Attached is a draft SOW that reflects the scope for EU data residency, APAC standby nodes, and the cross-region failover runbook we discussed. Key items to review: capacity tiers (tab: Capacity_Table_Q3.xlsx), SLA uplift during cutover, and the billing cadence for reserved capacity.

Action items I propose for this week:
1) Procurement: confirm legal & SOC 2 audit window so we can finalize the residency appendix
2) Engineering (Redwood): sizing confirmation and commit to standby node schedule by EOD Friday
3) Medica: provide any internal IP allowlist and compliance contacts for KYC evidence

If that aligns, I’ll update the SOW and send a DocuSign link for signatures.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124
[attachment: Medica_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 178KB)]

From: Elena Popov <elena.popov@medica-eu.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:42:00 +0200
Subject: Re: EU residency + APAC standby: renewal SOW & capacity readiness

Hi Ben —

Thanks for pulling this together. A few clarifications from our side:

- Go-live: 2027-07-15 preferred (we need two extra weeks for regional QA)
- Failover RTO: our internal requirement is 60s, not 90s — can Redwood commit to that for critical routes?
- Procurement: I’ve looped in our procurement alias (procurement@medica-eu.com) and copied our cloud compliance lead (see CC). They’ll need the SOC 2 evidence and the data flow diagrams.

On capacity: the marketing team expects a 50% uplift in token usage for the first 6 weeks post-launch due to a promotional drive; can you reflect a Q3 ramp (baseline +50%) in the capacity table?

Please also confirm if we can maintain EU data residency for logs and KV cache for EU-bound requests — that’s non-negotiable for our legal team.

Regards,
Elena Popov
Head of Platform Operations — Medica Health Systems
elena.popov@medica-eu.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Popov <elena.popov@medica-eu.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EU residency + APAC standby: renewal SOW & capacity readiness

Elena — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers now, detail in the attached spreadsheet and SOW v3.

- Go-live: 2027-07-15 OK — we’ll shift the cutover windows and coordinate QA days.
- RTO: 60s for critical routes is achievable with a small config change and a warmed KV cache; I’ll escalate to infra and confirm the micro-config that guarantees it.
- Residency: yes — logs and KV cache for EU-origin requests will remain within the EU tenant; we’ll include the residency appendix and the data flow diagram for procurement.
- Capacity: will update the Capacity_Table_Q3.xlsx to baseline +50% ramp with a 6-week smoothing period; Marcus will add buffer headroom for burst.

Next steps: Marcus and Soojin — can you confirm the infra attachment plan (node sizing, warm-standby snapshot cadence) and a hard date for when we can lock pricing for the reserved capacity? I’ll turn the SOW into a signable DocuSign after that.

Ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Popov <elena.popov@medica-eu.com>, Procurement <procurement@medica-eu.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 13:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EU residency + APAC standby: renewal SOW & capacity readiness

Ben / Soojin — internal ops note and reply to Medica.

Summary of infra commitments we can make in SOW v3:
- EU primary: dedicated (reserved) pool of 4x A100-equivalent instances, warm KV cache with daily snapshot and intra-day incremental checkpoints (retained in EU tenant).
- APAC standby: 2x A10/A30 equivalent nodes in APAC region configured as warm-standby with automated health polls; failover switch expected < 60s for prioritized routes (we’ll document route weightings).
- Burst policy: automatic short-term burst available for 48 hours beyond reserved commit; billing on a blended rate — see Capacity_Table_Q3.xlsx.
- Lock-in for pricing: we can hold quoted reserved pricing for 14 days after sign-off; for longer holds we need a small uplift to hedge capacity risk.

I updated the Capacity_Table_Q3.xlsx (attached) with the +50% ramp and included a conservative 20% buffer to protect against traffic spikes.

Elena / Procurement: If these commitments meet your legal/compliance needs we’ll:
1) Finalize residency appendix and data flow diagram by Monday 10 May.
2) Issue updated SOW and DocuSign link.

Marcus Lin
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
[attachment: Capacity_Table_Q3.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)]
